name: Pasur
description: Pasur is an Iranian fishing game where captures are made by exact rank pairing or by making sums of 11. Players score for aces, jacks, key cards, most clubs, and table-clearing surs, racing to 62 points.

overview.description: Pasur is an Iranian fishing game where captures are made by exact rank pairing or by making sums of 11. Players score for aces, jacks, key cards, most clubs, and table-clearing surs, racing to 62 points.

history.origins: Pasur is one of the best-known Iranian card games and belongs to the fishing family. It is traditionally played with a standard 52-card deck and is known by several local names.
timeline: Traditional era: Pasur develops as a popular social card game in Iran.
Late 20th century: Regional naming conventions such as Chahar barg and Haft khaj remain in active use.
21st century: Online rule references and web archives document standardized scoring and sur conventions.
history.cultural: The game is a common household and cafe game in Iran; in modern colloquial use, 'pasur' can also refer broadly to card play.
history.evolution: Core capture logic stayed stable while table conventions vary on target score (61, 62, or 100) and sur restrictions.

setup.players: 2 to 4 players. Two-player is standard; 4-player partnership is common with partners opposite.
setup.dealing: Deal anticlockwise in packets of 4: four to each player face down, then four face up to the tableau. If tableau starts with more than one jack, more than two queens, or more than two kings, redeal. If exactly one jack appears in tableau, bury it and replace from stock. After all players play their 4 cards, deal 4 more to each player; no new tableau cards are added. Continue until deck is exhausted.
setup.equipment: Cards and a visible running score.

rules.objective: Be the first player or team to reach at least 62 cumulative points.
rules.gameplay: Players act anticlockwise, playing one card from hand to the tableau. A played card either captures cards (played card plus captured cards move to that player's capture pile) or remains on tableau if no legal capture is taken. Face cards capture by rank (Q takes Q, K takes K). Number cards A-10 capture any chosen set of tableau cards summing with the played card to 11. Jacks capture all tableau cards except kings and queens. At end of final deal, remaining tableau cards go to the last player who made a capture.
keyRules: If your played card can capture, you must take one legal capture set; if multiple sets are legal, you choose one.
A sur is scored by clearing the tableau with a non-jack capture, except where sur restrictions apply.
Playing a jack never scores a sur, even if it clears the tableau.
No sur can be scored in the final deal after the last cards are dealt.
A side at 50 or more points cannot score a new sur or cancel an opponent sur.

strategy.basic: Prioritize captures that win clubs and key scoring cards (2 of Clubs, 10 of Diamonds). Avoid leaving easy 11-combinations for opponents.
strategy.intermediate: Manage tableau totals: leaving 10 or less often invites an opponent sur. Use face cards to break arithmetic capture patterns when you cannot profitably capture.
strategy.advanced: Track club majority race and sur state simultaneously. In two-player games, preserving jack timing can force opponent exposure and improve end-control for last-capture advantage.
tips: 7+ clubs is a large swing (7 points), so avoid donating clubs to tableau unless it creates a high-value capture.
When multiple captures are possible, choose the line that removes opponent sur threats and secures scoring cards.
Use end-of-round memory of who last captured to plan who receives leftover tableau cards.

scoring.description: At round end score captured cards and sur markers: 7 points for clubs majority (Haft Khaj), 1 each Ace, 1 each Jack, 2 for 2 of Clubs, 3 for 10 of Diamonds, and 5 per sur.
scoring.winCondition: First player or team with 62 or more cumulative points wins; if multiple reach 62+ simultaneously, highest score wins and ties continue.

synthesis.shortDescription: Iranian fishing game where players capture by rank or sum-to-11 and race to 62 through clubs, key cards, and sur bonuses.
